fullDescription.text: A local variable (VAR, VAR_TEMP, VAR_STAT, VAR_INST) is declared but never read or written by any code, initial value or declaration in the project.

help.text: A local variable (VAR, VAR_TEMP, VAR_STAT, VAR_INST) is declared but never read or written by any code, initial value or declaration in the project.
help.markdown:
## Description

A local variable (VAR, VAR_TEMP, VAR_STAT, VAR_INST) is declared but never read or written by any code, initial
value or declaration in the project.

Siemens SCL: static variables live in the instance DB, which HMIs and other PLCs may access, so they are reported only
when the declaration hides them with `{ ExternalAccessible := 'False' }`. Temporaries and constants are always
checked; data block members are never reported.

## Rationale

Unused declarations make a POU harder to read and suggest unfinished or dead logic; they also use memory. PLCopen
Coding Guidelines rule CP24 *Do not declare variables that are not used*.

Not reported, because something outside the parsed code may use the variable: variables with an attribute pragma
(HMI, OPC UA or ADS exposure), variables with an `AT` address (I/O mapping), names matching `sparePattern`, and every
variable of a POU with a graphical or unparsable body. Inputs and outputs are interface, not locals, and are not
checked here.

Rockwell (L5X): every tag carries `ExternalAccess`. Tags an HMI can read or write (`Read/Write`, `Read Only`) are
not reported; tags with `None` are. A base tag used only through an alias tag counts as used.

## Noncompliant

```st
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_Pump
VAR_INPUT
    bStart : BOOL;
END_VAR
VAR
    bRunning : BOOL;
    nOldCounter : INT;
END_VAR
bRunning := bStart;
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK
```

## Compliant

```st
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_Pump
VAR_INPUT
    bStart : BOOL;
END_VAR
VAR
    bRunning : BOOL;
    nSpare1 : INT;
END_VAR
bRunning := bStart;
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK
```

fullDescription.text: A CASE statement has no ELSE branch, so an unexpected selector value silently does nothing.

help.text: A CASE statement has no ELSE branch, so an unexpected selector value silently does nothing.
help.markdown:
## Description

A CASE statement has no ELSE branch, so an unexpected selector value silently does nothing.

## Rationale

State machines are usually written as CASE statements. If the state variable takes a value no branch handles (a new
state, a corrupted value, a bad HMI write), the machine stops in an undefined state without any alarm. An ELSE branch
makes that case explicit: raise an error or go to a safe state. PLCopen rule L17 asks the same for IF; the guidelines
have no CASE rule, so no PLCopen id is given.

A CASE on an enumeration that handles every value is not reported by default.

## Noncompliant

```st
PROGRAM P_Sequence
VAR
    nStep : INT;
END_VAR
CASE nStep OF
    0: nStep := 10;
    10: nStep := 0;
END_CASE
END_PROGRAM
```

## Compliant

```st
PROGRAM P_Sequence
VAR
    nStep : INT;
    bFault : BOOL;
END_VAR
CASE nStep OF
    0: nStep := 10;
    10: nStep := 0;
ELSE
    bFault := TRUE;
END_CASE
END_PROGRAM
```

fullDescription.text: A REAL or LREAL value is compared with `=` or `<>`.

help.text: A REAL or LREAL value is compared with `=` or `<>`.
help.markdown:
## Description

A REAL or LREAL value is compared with `=` or `<>`.

## Rationale

Floating-point values carry rounding errors, so a computed value is rarely exactly equal to another; the comparison
may never become TRUE (a sequence that never advances) or flicker. Compare the difference against a tolerance
instead. PLCopen Coding Guidelines rule CP8 *Floating point comparison shall not be equality or inequality*.

Comparisons with zero are not reported by default (CP8 lists them as its exception: a value set to 0.0 compares
exactly), nor is `x = x`, the usual test for NaN.

A value compared with its own copy (`IF a <> last THEN last := a;`, ladder `NEQ(a,last) MOV(a,last)`) is change
detection, exact by construction, and not reported. Rockwell (L5X): comparing two tags that no code of the program
or AOI writes (`EQU(Cfg_InpMax,Cfg_InpMin)` to flag an empty range) compares settings and is not reported either.

Ladder (Rockwell) findings are `info` by default: in ladder, exact REAL comparisons are mostly sentinel and
configuration checks. Raise them with `dialects: {rockwell: {severity: {PLCA-Q003: warning}}}` in `plca.yaml`.

## Noncompliant

```st
FUNCTION F_AtTarget : BOOL
VAR_INPUT
    rPosition : REAL;
    rTarget : REAL;
END_VAR
F_AtTarget := rPosition = rTarget;
END_FUNCTION
```

## Compliant

```st
FUNCTION F_AtTarget : BOOL
VAR_INPUT
    rPosition : REAL;
    rTarget : REAL;
END_VAR
F_AtTarget := ABS(rPosition - rTarget) < 0.001;
END_FUNCTION
```

fullDescription.text: The divisor of `/`, `MOD`, `DIV(…)` or `MOD(…)` is a literal or constant that evaluates to zero.

help.text: The divisor of `/`, `MOD`, `DIV(…)` or `MOD(…)` is a literal or constant that evaluates to zero.
help.markdown:
## Description

The divisor of `/`, `MOD`, `DIV(…)` or `MOD(…)` is a literal or constant that evaluates to zero.

## Rationale

An integer division by zero raises an exception on most runtimes and stops the PLC; a REAL division yields infinity
or NaN that spreads through the calculation. A divisor that is always zero is a bug, often a constant that was
changed or not yet set.

## Noncompliant

```st
FUNCTION F_Average : INT
VAR_INPUT
    nSum : INT;
END_VAR
VAR CONSTANT
    cSamples : INT := 0;
END_VAR
F_Average := nSum / cSamples;
END_FUNCTION
```

## Compliant

```st
FUNCTION F_Average : INT
VAR_INPUT
    nSum : INT;
END_VAR
VAR CONSTANT
    cSamples : INT := 8;
END_VAR
F_Average := nSum / cSamples;
END_FUNCTION
```

shortDescription.text: FOR loop variable modified in the loop body

fullDescription.text: The control variable of a FOR loop is assigned inside the loop body, passed to an output or VAR_IN_OUT parameter, or reused as the control variable of a nested FOR.

help.text: The control variable of a FOR loop is assigned inside the loop body, passed to an output or VAR_IN_OUT parameter, or reused as the control variable of a nested FOR.
help.markdown:
## Description

The control variable of a FOR loop is assigned inside the loop body, passed to an output or VAR_IN_OUT parameter, or
reused as the control variable of a nested FOR.

## Rationale

IEC 61131-3 says the control variable shall not be altered by the repeated statements. Changing it makes the number
of iterations unpredictable and can cause an endless loop, which trips the task watchdog. Use WHILE or REPEAT when
the iteration count is not known in advance. PLCopen Coding Guidelines rule *Loop variables should not be modified
inside a FOR loop*: the rule section says L12, the document's table of contents says L22.

## Noncompliant

```st
FUNCTION F_FindFirst : INT
VAR_INPUT
    aValues : ARRAY[1..10] OF INT;
END_VAR
VAR
    i : INT;
END_VAR
F_FindFirst := 0;
FOR i := 1 TO 10 DO
    IF aValues[i] > 0 THEN
        F_FindFirst := i;
        i := 10;
    END_IF
END_FOR
END_FUNCTION
```

## Compliant

```st
FUNCTION F_FindFirst : INT
VAR_INPUT
    aValues : ARRAY[1..10] OF INT;
END_VAR
VAR
    i : INT;
END_VAR
F_FindFirst := 0;
FOR i := 1 TO 10 DO
    IF aValues[i] > 0 THEN
        F_FindFirst := i;
        EXIT;
    END_IF
END_FOR
END_FUNCTION
```

fullDescription.text: A VAR_INPUT of a function, function block or method is written inside that POU (or a method or action of it).

help.text: A VAR_INPUT of a function, function block or method is written inside that POU (or a method or action of it).
help.markdown:
## Description

A VAR_INPUT of a function, function block or method is written inside that POU (or a method or action of it).

## Rationale

Inputs are set by the caller on every call. Overwriting one inside the POU hides the caller's value, and the effect
depends on whether the caller passes the input on the next call; for function blocks the changed value can also be
read back from outside. Copy the input to a local variable and change that. PLCopen Coding Guidelines rule CP17
*Usage of parameters shall match their declaration mode* ("each input parameter should not be written"). Writes
through a POINTER or REFERENCE input change the caller's data and are not reported.

Rockwell (L5X) Add-On Instructions: writing a constant to an input is a documented idiom — clearing a command an HMI
or program set (`OTU(PCmd_Start)`), or replacing an invalid setting by a default (`LEQ(Rate,0) MOV(1000,Rate)`) — and
is not reported; other writes are.

## Noncompliant

```st
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_Scale
VAR_INPUT
    rRaw : REAL;
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    rScaled : REAL;
END_VAR
IF rRaw < 0.0 THEN
    rRaw := 0.0;
END_IF
rScaled := rRaw * 0.1;
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK
```

## Compliant

```st
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_Scale
VAR_INPUT
    rRaw : REAL;
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    rScaled : REAL;
END_VAR
VAR
    rClamped : REAL;
END_VAR
rClamped := MAX(rRaw, 0.0);
rScaled := rClamped * 0.1;
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK
```

fullDescription.text: A POU calls itself, directly or through a chain of other POUs (functions, methods, actions, FB bodies, property accessors).

help.text: A POU calls itself, directly or through a chain of other POUs (functions, methods, actions, FB bodies, property accessors).
help.markdown:
## Description

A POU calls itself, directly or through a chain of other POUs (functions, methods, actions, FB bodies, property
accessors).

## Rationale

Each recursive call uses stack space, and PLC stacks are small and fixed; deep recursion can stop the controller.
Support for recursion also differs between vendors, so the code is less portable. Replace the recursion with a loop.
PLCopen Coding Guidelines rule CP13 *POUs shall not call themselves directly or indirectly*.

Cycles through a name that is declared more than once (overloaded methods in SIMATIC AX, duplicate copies of a POU)
are not reported, because which declaration a call refers to is not known.

## Noncompliant

```st
FUNCTION F_Factorial : DINT
VAR_INPUT
    n : DINT;
END_VAR
IF n <= 1 THEN
    F_Factorial := 1;
ELSE
    F_Factorial := n * F_Factorial(n - 1);
END_IF
END_FUNCTION
```

## Compliant

```st
FUNCTION F_Factorial : DINT
VAR_INPUT
    n : DINT;
END_VAR
VAR
    i : DINT;
END_VAR
F_Factorial := 1;
FOR i := 2 TO n DO
    F_Factorial := F_Factorial * i;
END_FOR
END_FUNCTION
```

fullDescription.text: An output-like variable — a physical output (`AT %Q…`), a global variable, or the POU's own VAR_OUTPUT — is written unconditionally in more than one place, so only the last write of each cycle takes effect.

help.text: An output-like variable — a physical output (`AT %Q…`), a global variable, or the POU's own VAR_OUTPUT — is written unconditionally in more than one place, so only the last write of each cycle takes effect.
help.markdown:
## Description

An output-like variable — a physical output (`AT %Q…`), a global variable, or the POU's own VAR_OUTPUT — is written
unconditionally in more than one place, so only the last write of each cycle takes effect.

## Rationale

This is the structured-text form of the ladder "double coil": two rungs driving the same coil. The earlier write is
dead, the behaviour depends on execution order, and the logic that decides the output is spread over the
application. Compute the value once, in one place. PLCopen Coding Guidelines rule CP12 *Physical outputs shall be
written once per PLC cycle* covers physical outputs; this rule also checks globals and FB outputs.

To stay quiet on correct code, only unconditional writes count (`:=` or `=>` in a top-level statement of a body),
`S=`/`R=` latches, read-modify-write statements (`n := n + 1`) and writes inside IF/CASE/loops are ignored, and a
second write in the same body is not reported when the variable is read in between (sequential use of a working
variable).

In ladder (Rockwell L5X) an `OTE` is a coil by definition: it counts even when its rung reads the coil (seal-in) and
whatever happens between two OTEs, for any tag — the "duplicate destructive bit" check Studio 5000's verification
warns about. Across routines only OTE coils are compared, since routines are often called conditionally as
alternatives; an AOI's Prescan/Postscan/EnableInFalse routines are never compared with its logic (they run instead of
it), and outputs of AOI calls do not count (a required AOI output must be bound to a tag, often a scratch tag). Tags
whose name matches `sparePattern` are exempt.

## Noncompliant

```st
PROGRAM P_Conveyor
VAR
    bStart : BOOL;
    bJog : BOOL;
    qMotor AT %QX0.0 : BOOL;
END_VAR
qMotor := bStart;
qMotor := bJog;
END_PROGRAM
```

## Compliant

```st
PROGRAM P_Conveyor
VAR
    bStart : BOOL;
    bJog : BOOL;
    qMotor AT %QX0.0 : BOOL;
END_VAR
qMotor := bStart OR bJog;
END_PROGRAM
```

fullDescription.text: A direct address such as `%IX0.1`, `%QW4` or `%MD10` is used in code instead of a symbolic variable.

help.text: A direct address such as `%IX0.1`, `%QW4` or `%MD10` is used in code instead of a symbolic variable.
help.markdown:
## Description

A direct address such as `%IX0.1`, `%QW4` or `%MD10` is used in code instead of a symbolic variable.

## Rationale

A bare address says nothing about what it is, makes the code depend on one hardware layout, and is easily missed when
the I/O configuration changes. Declare a variable with `AT %…` once and use its name. PLCopen Coding Guidelines rule
N1 *Avoid physical addresses*.

Siemens SCL: absolute operands (`%I0.0`, `%DB1.DBX0.0`, classic `DB10.DBW2`) and ANY pointers (`P#DB1.DBX0.0 BYTE
10`) are reported; use a PLC tag (`"Start_Button"`) or a data block member (`"DB_IO".Valve`) instead.

Rockwell (L5X) has no direct addresses; the equivalent is logic on raw module tags (`Local:1:I.Data.5`,
`Rack1:2:O.Data[0]`). They are reported except in routines that only map I/O (every rung a contact driving a coil, a
`MOV`/`COP`, or every ST statement a plain assignment) and when a whole module tag is handed to a device AOI
(`PF755_Drive(Pump, Pump:I, Pump:O, …)`), the device-object form Rockwell recommends. Alias tags of module points are
the compliant form. Controller status flags (`S:FS`) are not I/O.

## Noncompliant

```st
PROGRAM P_Lamp
%QX0.1 := %IX0.0;
END_PROGRAM
```

## Compliant

```st
PROGRAM P_Lamp
VAR
    iButton AT %IX0.0 : BOOL;
    qLamp AT %QX0.1 : BOOL;
END_VAR
qLamp := iButton;
END_PROGRAM
```

fullDescription.text: A string literal is used as a password, token or other secret (assigned to, initialising, passed as or compared with a variable or parameter whose name matches `namePattern`), or a string literal is an IPv4 address.

help.text: A string literal is used as a password, token or other secret (assigned to, initialising, passed as or compared with a variable or parameter whose name matches `namePattern`), or a string literal is an IPv4 address.
help.markdown:
## Description

A string literal is used as a password, token or other secret (assigned to, initialising, passed as or compared with
a variable or parameter whose name matches `namePattern`), or a string literal is an IPv4 address.

## Rationale

Credentials in the PLC program are visible to anyone who can read the project or upload it from the controller,
cannot be rotated without a program change, and are often identical across machines. A password check against a
literal is a back door. Hard-coded IP addresses tie the program to one network layout and hide communication
partners from reviews. Keep secrets in a protected store and network settings in configuration.

Not reported: empty strings and masks such as `'*****'`, loopback addresses and netmasks, and dotted numbers given to
a version-like name (`sVersion := '1.0.0.0'`, `sFirmwareRev`), which look like IPv4 addresses but are not.

## Noncompliant

```st
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_Login
VAR_INPUT
    sUser : STRING;
    sPassword : STRING;
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    bAuthorized : BOOL;
END_VAR
VAR
    sServerIp : STRING := '192.168.10.20';
END_VAR
bAuthorized := sUser = 'service' AND sPassword = 'Service#2024';
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK
```

## Compliant

```st
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_Login
VAR_INPUT
    sUser : STRING;
    sPassword : STRING;
    sExpectedHash : STRING;
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    bAuthorized : BOOL;
END_VAR
bAuthorized := F_Hash(sPassword) = sExpectedHash;
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK
```

fullDescription.text: Code that can never run: statements after `RETURN`, `EXIT`, `CONTINUE` or `JMP` in the same statement list, an IF, ELSIF or WHILE whose condition is always FALSE, ELSIF/ELSE branches after a condition that is always TRUE, and Rockwell rungs disabled by an `AFI` instruction.

help.text: Code that can never run: statements after `RETURN`, `EXIT`, `CONTINUE` or `JMP` in the same statement list, an IF, ELSIF or WHILE whose condition is always FALSE, ELSIF/ELSE branches after a condition that is always TRUE, and Rockwell rungs disabled by an `AFI` instruction.
help.markdown:
## Description

Code that can never run: statements after `RETURN`, `EXIT`, `CONTINUE` or `JMP` in the same statement list, an IF,
ELSIF or WHILE whose condition is always FALSE, ELSIF/ELSE branches after a condition that is always TRUE, and
Rockwell rungs disabled by an `AFI` instruction.

## Rationale

Dead code misleads the reader, who must work out that it never runs, and often hides a mistake: a `RETURN` left over
from debugging, or logic switched off with `IF FALSE THEN` and forgotten. PLCopen Coding Guidelines rule CP2 *All code
shall be used in the application*.

Only conditions built from literals are reported by default. A condition on a named constant (`IF cSimulation THEN`)
is usually a deliberate configuration switch; set `includeNamedConstants` to report those too. A label after a jump
makes the following code reachable again. TwinCAT's `RETURN(expression)` is not treated as an unconditional exit. Conditions generated from ladder, FBD and SFC are not checked, but a rung
whose main series contains `AFI` is reported: it is switched off for good.

## Noncompliant

```st
FUNCTION F_Limit : INT
VAR_INPUT
    nValue : INT;
END_VAR
F_Limit := nValue;
RETURN;
IF nValue > 100 THEN
    F_Limit := 100;
END_IF
END_FUNCTION
```

```st
PROGRAM P_Test
VAR
    bPump : BOOL;
END_VAR
IF FALSE THEN
    bPump := TRUE;
END_IF
END_PROGRAM
```

## Compliant

```st
FUNCTION F_Limit : INT
VAR_INPUT
    nValue : INT;
END_VAR
F_Limit := nValue;
IF nValue > 100 THEN
    F_Limit := 100;
END_IF
END_FUNCTION
```

fullDescription.text: A WHILE or REPEAT loop whose condition is constant (`WHILE TRUE`, `UNTIL FALSE`) or reads only variables that the loop body never changes, and whose body has no `EXIT`, `RETURN` or `JMP` out of the loop.

help.text: A WHILE or REPEAT loop whose condition is constant (`WHILE TRUE`, `UNTIL FALSE`) or reads only variables that the loop body never changes, and whose body has no `EXIT`, `RETURN` or `JMP` out of the loop.
help.markdown:
## Description

A WHILE or REPEAT loop whose condition is constant (`WHILE TRUE`, `UNTIL FALSE`) or reads only variables that the loop
body never changes, and whose body has no `EXIT`, `RETURN` or `JMP` out of the loop.

## Rationale

A PLC program runs inside a cyclic task: a loop that never ends keeps the cycle from finishing, the watchdog trips and
the controller stops, with every output in its fault state. Waiting for an input inside a loop never works either —
inputs are only read between cycles. Change the condition inside the loop, add an iteration limit, or restructure the
wait as a step of a state machine that is checked once per cycle.

Not reported when the loop may end in ways the analysis cannot see: the condition calls a function, method or
property or assigns a variable, reads through a pointer, reference or VAR_IN_OUT, or reads a global, an instance member
or a function block instance while the body calls other code; or a variable it reads has its address taken anywhere in
the POU.

## Noncompliant

```st
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_Wait
VAR_INPUT
    bReady : BOOL;
END_VAR
VAR
    nTries : INT;
END_VAR
WHILE NOT bReady DO
    nTries := nTries + 1;
END_WHILE
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK
```

## Compliant

```st
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_Wait
VAR_INPUT
    bReady : BOOL;
END_VAR
VAR
    nTries : INT;
END_VAR
WHILE NOT bReady AND nTries < 10 DO
    nTries := nTries + 1;
END_WHILE
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK
```

fullDescription.text: A POU body nests IF, CASE, FOR, WHILE or REPEAT statements deeper than `maxNesting`, or its cyclomatic complexity is above `maxComplexity`. Complexity is 1 plus one for every IF/ELSIF condition, CASE branch, FOR, WHILE and REPEAT.

help.text: A POU body nests IF, CASE, FOR, WHILE or REPEAT statements deeper than `maxNesting`, or its cyclomatic complexity is above `maxComplexity`. Complexity is 1 plus one for every IF/ELSIF condition, CASE branch, FOR, WHILE and REPEAT.
help.markdown:
## Description

A POU body nests IF, CASE, FOR, WHILE or REPEAT statements deeper than `maxNesting`, or its cyclomatic complexity is
above `maxComplexity`. Complexity is 1 plus one for every IF/ELSIF condition, CASE branch, FOR, WHILE and REPEAT.

## Rationale

Deeply nested and highly branched code is hard to read, review and test, and is where commissioning changes go wrong.
PLCopen Coding Guidelines rule CP9 *Limit the complexity of POU code*. Split the logic into methods, actions or
functions, or replace nested IFs with a CASE state machine. The limits are parameters; CODESYS and TwinCAT ship their
own metric checks off by default, and so this rule reports at `info`.

Bodies generated from ladder, FBD and SFC are not measured: a ladder routine is a list of rungs, and each rung's
lowered conditions are not nesting the engineer wrote.

## Noncompliant

```st
FUNCTION F_Deep : INT
VAR_INPUT
    a, b, c, d, e, f : BOOL;
END_VAR
IF a THEN
    IF b THEN
        IF c THEN
            IF d THEN
                IF e THEN
                    IF f THEN
                        F_Deep := 1;
                    END_IF
                END_IF
            END_IF
        END_IF
    END_IF
END_IF
END_FUNCTION
```

## Compliant

```st
FUNCTION F_Flat : INT
VAR_INPUT
    a, b, c, d, e, f : BOOL;
END_VAR
IF a AND b AND c AND d AND e AND f THEN
    F_Flat := 1;
END_IF
END_FUNCTION
```

fullDescription.text: A jump: ST `JMP`, Siemens SCL `GOTO`, a jump in a PLCopen LD/FBD network, or a Rockwell ladder `JMP`.

help.text: A jump: ST `JMP`, Siemens SCL `GOTO`, a jump in a PLCopen LD/FBD network, or a Rockwell ladder `JMP`.
help.markdown:
## Description

A jump: ST `JMP`, Siemens SCL `GOTO`, a jump in a PLCopen LD/FBD network, or a Rockwell ladder `JMP`.

## Rationale

Jumps make the order of execution hard to follow. In ladder they are worse: the rungs a `JMP` skips are not scanned,
so their outputs keep their last state, which is easy to miss when reading the logic. PLCopen Coding Guidelines rule
CP19 *Usage of Jump and Return should be avoided*. Use IF, CASE or loops in text languages and explicit conditions in
ladder. One finding per jump; the label is not reported separately.

## Noncompliant

```st
PROGRAM P_Jump
VAR
    nStep : INT;
END_VAR
IF nStep = 0 THEN
    JMP lEnd;
END_IF
nStep := nStep + 1;
lEnd:
END_PROGRAM
```

## Compliant

```st
PROGRAM P_Jump
VAR
    nStep : INT;
END_VAR
IF nStep <> 0 THEN
    nStep := nStep + 1;
END_IF
END_PROGRAM
```

fullDescription.text: A program, function block, function, class or Rockwell routine that nothing runs: it is not scheduled in a task, not called, not instantiated and not referenced from code that runs.

help.text: A program, function block, function, class or Rockwell routine that nothing runs: it is not scheduled in a task, not called, not instantiated and not referenced from code that runs.
help.markdown:
## Description

A program, function block, function, class or Rockwell routine that nothing runs: it is not scheduled in a task,
not called, not instantiated and not referenced from code that runs.

## Rationale

Code that never runs still has to be read, reviewed and maintained, and a routine that was meant to run but is not
called (a missing `JSR`, a program left out of the task) is a bug that testing on site may not reveal. PLCopen Coding
Guidelines rule CP2 *All code shall be used in the application*.

Reachability starts at the entry points: the programs of the configured tasks and Siemens organisation blocks. From
there it follows calls, `JSR`s, instance declarations (anywhere, including global variable lists and structures),
`EXTENDS`/`IMPLEMENTS` and references to POUs in expressions. Methods, actions and properties are not reported on their
own.

The rule needs a complete export to be right, so it stays silent when it cannot see every caller: code without a task
configuration (or, for Siemens, without an OB), a dialect with bodies in a language that is not parsed (LD, FBD, CFC;
Rockwell FBD and SFC routines silence their program), and Siemens code that calls instance data blocks the export does
not contain. Names declared twice, the CODESYS implicit check functions (`CheckBounds`, `CheckPointer`, …) and a dialect
in which most POUs are unused — a library bundled with a small test program — are not reported either.

## Noncompliant

```st
PROGRAM P_Main
VAR
    nCount : INT;
END_VAR
nCount := F_Used(nCount);
END_PROGRAM

FUNCTION F_Used : INT
VAR_INPUT
    n : INT;
END_VAR
F_Used := n + 1;
END_FUNCTION

FUNCTION F_Forgotten : INT
VAR_INPUT
    n : INT;
END_VAR
F_Forgotten := n - 1;
END_FUNCTION

CONFIGURATION Cfg
    RESOURCE Res ON PLC
        TASK tMain(INTERVAL := T#10MS, PRIORITY := 1);
        PROGRAM iMain WITH tMain : P_Main;
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION
```

## Compliant

```st
PROGRAM P_Main
VAR
    nCount : INT;
END_VAR
nCount := F_Used(nCount);
END_PROGRAM

FUNCTION F_Used : INT
VAR_INPUT
    n : INT;
END_VAR
F_Used := n + 1;
END_FUNCTION

CONFIGURATION Cfg
    RESOURCE Res ON PLC
        TASK tMain(INTERVAL := T#10MS, PRIORITY := 1);
        PROGRAM iMain WITH tMain : P_Main;
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION
```

shortDescription.text: Function block instance called more than once per cycle

fullDescription.text: The same function block instance — a timer, counter, edge detector or user FB — is called more than once in a cycle: twice in one body (not as alternatives in different IF/CASE branches), or from two programs, function blocks or routines when the instance is global. Rockwell: the same TIMER in two TON/TOF/RTO instructions, or the same COUNTER in two CTU (or two CTD) instructions.

help.text: The same function block instance — a timer, counter, edge detector or user FB — is called more than once in a cycle: twice in one body (not as alternatives in different IF/CASE branches), or from two programs, function blocks or routines when the instance is global. Rockwell: the same TIMER in two TON/TOF/RTO instructions, or the same COUNTER in two CTU (or two CTD) instructions.
help.markdown:
## Description

The same function block instance — a timer, counter, edge detector or user FB — is called more than once in a cycle:
twice in one body (not as alternatives in different IF/CASE branches), or from two programs, function blocks or
routines when the instance is global. Rockwell: the same TIMER in two TON/TOF/RTO instructions, or the same COUNTER in
two CTU (or two CTD) instructions.

## Rationale

A function block keeps state between calls and expects to be called once per cycle. A second call works on what the
first left behind: a timer called with two different IN values restarts or never elapses, an R_TRIG sees no edge, a
counter counts twice. In ladder the second timer instruction runs even when its rung is false, and resets the timer.
PLCopen Coding Guidelines rule CP20 *Function block instances should be called only once*. Call the instance once and
use its outputs where needed.

Not compared: calls inside loops, calls through a variable array index (`afbAxis[i]()`), calls in SFC actions, where
the active step decides what runs, and `tmr(IN := FALSE)`, the usual way to reset a timer when a state machine changes
step. CTU and CTD on the same Rockwell counter form an up/down counter and are not reported. Rockwell Add-On
Instructions are not compared: Logix has no functions, so stateless AOIs are routinely called several times.

## Noncompliant

```st
PROGRAM P_Conveyor
VAR
    fbDelay : TON;
    bStart, bStop, bRun : BOOL;
END_VAR
fbDelay(IN := bStart, PT := T#2S);
IF fbDelay.Q THEN
    bRun := TRUE;
END_IF
fbDelay(IN := bStop, PT := T#5S);
END_PROGRAM
```

## Compliant

```st
PROGRAM P_Conveyor
VAR
    fbStartDelay : TON;
    fbStopDelay : TON;
    bStart, bStop, bRun : BOOL;
END_VAR
fbStartDelay(IN := bStart, PT := T#2S);
fbStopDelay(IN := bStop, PT := T#5S);
IF fbStartDelay.Q THEN
    bRun := TRUE;
END_IF
END_PROGRAM
```

shortDescription.text: Global variable written from several tasks

fullDescription.text: A global variable is written by code running in more than one task, according to the project's task configuration (IEC configurations, TwinCAT task objects, PLCopen instances, Rockwell tasks).

help.text: A global variable is written by code running in more than one task, according to the project's task configuration (IEC configurations, TwinCAT task objects, PLCopen instances, Rockwell tasks).
help.markdown:
## Description

A global variable is written by code running in more than one task, according to the project's task configuration
(IEC configurations, TwinCAT task objects, PLCopen instances, Rockwell tasks).

## Rationale

Tasks of different priority interrupt each other. If two tasks write the same global, one task can preempt the other
between reading and writing it, and an update is lost; a structure or string can be seen half written. PLCopen Coding
Guidelines rule CP10 *Avoid multiple writes from multiple tasks*. Let one task own the variable and hand data over
through separate variables, or use the runtime's synchronisation (CODESYS `SysSem`, TwinCAT `TestAndSet`).

The rule needs a task configuration with at least two tasks; without one it is silent. A POU runs in every task whose
programs call it, directly or indirectly; Siemens organisation blocks are tasks. Startup tasks (`startupTaskPattern`,
by default the TIA names of OB100–OB102) do not count, since they finish before the cyclic tasks start. One finding per
variable.

## Noncompliant

```st
VAR_GLOBAL
    gnParts : INT;
END_VAR

PROGRAM P_Fast
gnParts := gnParts + 1;
END_PROGRAM

PROGRAM P_Slow
gnParts := 0;
END_PROGRAM

CONFIGURATION Cfg
    RESOURCE Res ON PLC
        TASK tFast(INTERVAL := T#2MS, PRIORITY := 1);
        TASK tSlow(INTERVAL := T#100MS, PRIORITY := 10);
        PROGRAM iFast WITH tFast : P_Fast;
        PROGRAM iSlow WITH tSlow : P_Slow;
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION
```

## Compliant

```st
VAR_GLOBAL
    gnParts : INT;
    gbResetParts : BOOL;
END_VAR

PROGRAM P_Fast
IF gbResetParts THEN
    gnParts := 0;
ELSE
    gnParts := gnParts + 1;
END_IF
END_PROGRAM

PROGRAM P_Slow
gbResetParts := TRUE;
END_PROGRAM

CONFIGURATION Cfg
    RESOURCE Res ON PLC
        TASK tFast(INTERVAL := T#2MS, PRIORITY := 1);
        TASK tSlow(INTERVAL := T#100MS, PRIORITY := 10);
        PROGRAM iFast WITH tFast : P_Fast;
        PROGRAM iSlow WITH tSlow : P_Slow;
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION
```

fullDescription.text: A temporary variable without an initial value is read on some path before anything assigns it. Temporaries are the locals of functions, methods and property accessors, VAR_TEMP of any POU, and a function's result.

help.text: A temporary variable without an initial value is read on some path before anything assigns it. Temporaries are the locals of functions, methods and property accessors, VAR_TEMP of any POU, and a function's result.
help.markdown:
## Description

A temporary variable without an initial value is read on some path before anything assigns it. Temporaries are the
locals of functions, methods and property accessors, VAR_TEMP of any POU, and a function's result.

## Rationale

IEC 61131-3 sets every variable to its type's default before it is used, so nothing is ever undefined — but a
temporary starts from that default on every call. Code that reads it first usually expects the value of the last call
(which only a function block's static variable keeps) or forgot an assignment on one branch. On Siemens S7 classic
(non-optimised) blocks, temporaries are not initialised at all and hold whatever the stack held. PLCopen Coding
Guidelines rule CP3 *All variables shall be initialized before being used*.

The analysis follows the structure of the body: IF and CASE branches are merged, a loop body may run zero times
(REPEAT at least once), and RETURN, EXIT and CONTINUE end a path. Passing the variable as VAR_IN_OUT or to a call whose
parameters are not known (library code), taking its address or writing a part of it counts as an assignment. An
accumulator that builds on the default (`nSum := nSum + x`, `F := SHL(F, 1)`) is deliberate in CODESYS-style code and is
reported only for Siemens, where classic blocks do not initialise temporaries. Static variables of function blocks and programs are not checked:
keeping a value from one cycle to the next is what they are for. Structures and arrays, bodies with JMP or `__TRY`,
and Rockwell code (which has no temporaries) are not checked.

## Noncompliant

```st
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_Door
VAR_INPUT
    bOpenCmd : BOOL;
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    bMotor : BOOL;
END_VAR
VAR_TEMP
    bWasOpen : BOOL;
END_VAR
IF bOpenCmd AND NOT bWasOpen THEN
    bMotor := TRUE;
END_IF
bWasOpen := bOpenCmd;
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK
```

## Compliant

```st
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_Door
VAR_INPUT
    bOpenCmd : BOOL;
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    bMotor : BOOL;
END_VAR
VAR
    bWasOpen : BOOL;
END_VAR
IF bOpenCmd AND NOT bWasOpen THEN
    bMotor := TRUE;
END_IF
bWasOpen := bOpenCmd;
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK
```

fullDescription.text: A value is converted implicitly to a type that cannot hold every value of its own type: a wider integer or bit string to a narrower one (`DINT` to `INT`, `DWORD` to `WORD`), a real to an integer, or `LREAL` to `REAL` — in an assignment, an input argument or an output argument. Also an integer constant that does not fit the target type.

help.text: A value is converted implicitly to a type that cannot hold every value of its own type: a wider integer or bit string to a narrower one (`DINT` to `INT`, `DWORD` to `WORD`), a real to an integer, or `LREAL` to `REAL` — in an assignment, an input argument or an output argument. Also an integer constant that does not fit the target type.
help.markdown:
## Description

A value is converted implicitly to a type that cannot hold every value of its own type: a wider integer or bit string
to a narrower one (`DINT` to `INT`, `DWORD` to `WORD`), a real to an integer, or `LREAL` to `REAL` — in an assignment,
an input argument or an output argument. Also an integer constant that does not fit the target type.

## Rationale

Implicit narrowing silently truncates: a counter stored in an INT wraps at 32767, a REAL assigned to an INT loses its
fraction (and overflows above 32767), an LREAL position loses precision. Making the conversion explicit with a
conversion function shows the reader that the range was considered, and is where a LIMIT belongs. PLCopen Coding
Guidelines rule CP25 *Data types conversion should be explicit*.

Untyped literals take the type of the other operand (`nInt + 1` stays INT, `MAX(0.0, rSpeed)` stays REAL), so they
never cause a finding by themselves; named constants count by value, and one that fits is fine. Conversions between
signed and unsigned types of the same size, and from integers to reals, are not reported. Rockwell code is not
checked: Logix converts on assignment by design and has no conversion functions to make it explicit.

## Noncompliant

```st
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_Count
VAR_INPUT
    diPulses : DINT;
    rSpeed : REAL;
END_VAR
VAR
    nPulses : INT;
    nSpeed : INT;
END_VAR
nPulses := diPulses;
nSpeed := rSpeed;
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK
```

## Compliant

```st
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_Count
VAR_INPUT
    diPulses : DINT;
    rSpeed : REAL;
END_VAR
VAR
    nPulses : INT;
    nSpeed : INT;
END_VAR
nPulses := DINT_TO_INT(LIMIT(-32768, diPulses, 32767));
nSpeed := REAL_TO_INT(rSpeed);
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK
```

fullDescription.text: A pointer is dereferenced (`p^`) in a body that never compares it with 0, tests it with `__ISVALIDREF` or assigns it from `ADR(…)` before the dereference.

help.text: A pointer is dereferenced (`p^`) in a body that never compares it with 0, tests it with `__ISVALIDREF` or assigns it from `ADR(…)` before the dereference.
help.markdown:
## Description

A pointer is dereferenced (`p^`) in a body that never compares it with 0, tests it with `__ISVALIDREF` or assigns it
from `ADR(…)` before the dereference.

## Rationale

Dereferencing a null pointer raises an access violation and stops the PLC (CODESYS, TwinCAT); a stale or zero pointer
passed in by a caller is a classic cause of a controller crash after an online change. Check the pointer before using
it, or use a REFERENCE with `__ISVALIDREF`. The check is approximate: any comparison of the pointer with 0 earlier in
the body, or in a condition around the dereference, counts. A pointer member of a function block that the block's own
code assigns (in `FB_init` or a setter method) is treated as part of the object's contract and not reported. One
finding per pointer and body.

## Noncompliant

```st
FUNCTION F_Read : INT
VAR_INPUT
    pValue : POINTER TO INT;
END_VAR
F_Read := pValue^;
END_FUNCTION
```

## Compliant

```st
FUNCTION F_Read : INT
VAR_INPUT
    pValue : POINTER TO INT;
END_VAR
IF pValue <> 0 THEN
    F_Read := pValue^;
END_IF
END_FUNCTION
```

shortDescription.text: Externally writable value used without a check

fullDescription.text: A value that can be written from outside the PLC — by an HMI, a SCADA system or another network client — drives a physical output, or is used as an array index, with no range or validity check in between.

help.text: A value that can be written from outside the PLC — by an HMI, a SCADA system or another network client — drives a physical output, or is used as an array index, with no range or validity check in between.
help.markdown:
## Description

A value that can be written from outside the PLC — by an HMI, a SCADA system or another network client — drives a
physical output, or is used as an array index, with no range or validity check in between.

## Rationale

Anything an operator panel or network client can write must be treated as untrusted: a typing error, a misconfigured
HMI or an attacker can send any value. A setpoint passed straight to an analog output can drive the process outside
its limits; a command bit wired straight to an output bypasses every interlock; an index that is out of range faults
the controller (Rockwell major fault, CODESYS exception) or overwrites neighbouring data. *Top 20 Secure PLC Coding
Practices* (ISA GCA / admeritia, 2021), practice 8 "Validate HMI input variables at the PLC, not just at the HMI" and
practice 9 "Validate indirections".

Externally writable means: Rockwell controller and program tags with `ExternalAccess="Read/Write"` (the default) that no
logic of the project writes; Siemens data block members that are not `ExternalWritable := 'False'` and that no block
writes; in CODESYS, TwinCAT and PLCopen, where any symbol may be reachable, variables with an OPC UA attribute or whose
name or list name matches `externalPattern` (HMI, SCADA, VISU, OPC, remote).

A use counts as checked when the value is compared, limited (`LIMIT`, `MIN`, `MAX`, `SEL`, `MUX`, ladder `LIM`), used
as a CASE selector or overwritten earlier in the body or in a condition around the use. Only pass-through is reported:
an output assigned from the value and constants alone, or set under a condition on the value alone. An interlock in
the expression is a check and silences the finding.

## Noncompliant

```st
VAR_GLOBAL
    GVL_HMI_rSpeedSetpoint : REAL;
    GVL_HMI_nRecipe : INT;
END_VAR

PROGRAM P_Drive
VAR
    qrSpeedOut AT %QD4 : REAL;
    arRecipes : ARRAY[0..9] OF REAL;
    rRecipe : REAL;
END_VAR
qrSpeedOut := GVL_HMI_rSpeedSetpoint;
rRecipe := arRecipes[GVL_HMI_nRecipe];
END_PROGRAM
```

## Compliant

```st
VAR_GLOBAL
    GVL_HMI_rSpeedSetpoint : REAL;
    GVL_HMI_nRecipe : INT;
END_VAR

PROGRAM P_Drive
VAR
    qrSpeedOut AT %QD4 : REAL;
    arRecipes : ARRAY[0..9] OF REAL;
    rRecipe : REAL;
END_VAR
qrSpeedOut := LIMIT(0.0, GVL_HMI_rSpeedSetpoint, 1500.0);
IF GVL_HMI_nRecipe >= 0 AND GVL_HMI_nRecipe <= 9 THEN
    rRecipe := arRecipes[GVL_HMI_nRecipe];
END_IF
END_PROGRAM
```

fullDescription.text: Logic that waits for a moment or a value nobody sets by accident: a comparison with an absolute date, a real-time clock value compared with a calendar year, an equality comparison with a "magic" constant (hexspeak such as `16#DEADBEEF`, `16#C0FFEE`, or leet numbers such as 1337), or a timer that runs from start-up and fires only after a long delay.

help.text: Logic that waits for a moment or a value nobody sets by accident: a comparison with an absolute date, a real-time clock value compared with a calendar year, an equality comparison with a "magic" constant (hexspeak such as `16#DEADBEEF`, `16#C0FFEE`, or leet numbers such as 1337), or a timer that runs from start-up and fires only after a long delay.
help.markdown:
## Description

Logic that waits for a moment or a value nobody sets by accident: a comparison with an absolute date, a real-time clock
value compared with a calendar year, an equality comparison with a "magic" constant (hexspeak such as `16#DEADBEEF`,
`16#C0FFEE`, or leet numbers such as 1337), or a timer that runs from start-up and fires only after a long delay.

## Rationale

This is the shape of a logic bomb or a backdoor: code that behaves normally during commissioning and tests, and does
something else on a given date, after weeks of operation, or when a value only an insider knows is written. Such code
has been found in sabotage and research cases, and a code review is the best place to catch it. Each finding asks a
reviewer to confirm what the condition enables. Daily schedules (time-of-day comparisons) and short start-up delays are
normal and not reported.

Clock sources recognised: the IEC `RTC` block, CODESYS `SysTimeRtcGet`, TwinCAT `NT_GetTime`, `FB_LocalSystemTime`,
`F_GetSystemTime`, Siemens `RD_LOC_T`/`RD_SYS_T`, and Rockwell `GSV(WallClockTime, …)`.

## Noncompliant

```st
PROGRAM P_Pump
VAR
    fbClock : RTC;
    bRun : BOOL;
    nCode : DINT;
END_VAR
fbClock(EN := TRUE);
IF fbClock.CDT >= DT#2027-01-01-00:00:00 THEN
    bRun := FALSE;
END_IF
IF nCode = 16#DEADBEEF THEN
    bRun := TRUE;
END_IF
END_PROGRAM
```

## Compliant

```st
PROGRAM P_Pump
VAR
    fbClock : RTC;
    bRun : BOOL;
    bNight : BOOL;
END_VAR
fbClock(EN := TRUE);
bNight := DT_TO_TOD(fbClock.CDT) >= TOD#22:00:00;
bRun := NOT bNight;
END_PROGRAM
```

Exact floating-point comparison with '='; compare the difference against a tolerance, e.g. ABS(a - b) < eps
